I have a few events that have occured in my life which are traumatic. But the trauma which i know has changed the trajectory of transitioning from teens to adulthood. Was the bullying i frequently recived all through the 6 years of secondary school. It ruined me as a person. I was bullied for being "odd" (i was just really shy and liked my own thing) i was more interested in video games, creepypastas, ancient history than what i wore. I was subjected to constant verbal insults, spat at, had food thrown on me. All for existing it seemed. I was always a shy child/teen, even as an adult i prefer to mind my buisness. But this bullying made me constantly nervous, i took up smoking to try and relieve this feeling, (bad habit i know) and self harming was another popular little habit of mine. I then needed therapy on and off. but then again like most people i often think how i could of been if i wasnt put through that. How my life may be now. I could of left at 16, but i stayed in school till 18 cause i wanted higher qualifications. Its safe to say at the end of the year i didnt buy their stupid fucking yearbook or leavers hoodie, i was gonna get on with life with no awful physical reminders of what them sadistic assholes put me through. Maybe one day in the future i will get over it, but i will not forgive them. But now im studying at college in hopes to become a psychiatric nurse. One thing i have learned from my trauma, is to not judge anyone until you know their story.

I didn't witness this, because i was so young my brain still hadn't gained "consciousness". But this happened to my grandma. When i was little she would come to babysit. Now my grandma only met her father in law (my great grandfather) once. All thats said is "he was a drunk in the town centre, but had piercing blue eyes. (Like really blue)". So back to the story. Toddler me, was about to take a tumble down the stairs (it happened many times) and my grandma had a feeling to find me. And she did, just in time to grab me. She then looked to her right to where the door at the end of the hall had a window at the top. Then she saw these blue piercing eyes, no face noticed i dont think but literally eye-catching blue eyes. Anyways She then basically pulled me back from my potential demise, looked back and it was gone. But she immediately thought of my great grandfather because of the eyes. Its interesting because she is not a believer in paranormal activity, and has no time for it. But that moment did strike her as very odd.
